key_catalyst: Brent crude surges above $100 on Houthi tanker attacks and Trump Iran threats, pushing 10Y yields to 4.70% and 2Y to 17-month highs, compressing QQQ mega-cap valuations
reasoning: Three concurrent HIGH-severity catalysts are escalating simultaneously: Brent crude broke $100 for the first time since May with Goldman forecasting >$120 and RBC citing a path to $146, Alphabet and Tesla both reported first-ever negative free cash flow while massively raising AI capex (GOOGL $195-205B, TSLA >$25B), and Section 301 tariffs on 60 countries covering ~99% of US imports just went live with retaliation risk pending. The trajectory across the past four sessions shows clear escalation—oil from ~$90 (Jul 20) to $100+ (Jul 24), 10Y yields from 4.36% to 4.70%, and QQQ losses compounding (-1.90% then -1.37%)—indicating these catalysts are not yet fully absorbed and overnight gap-down risk is material.
